transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (BrightLift), Sara O'Neill (BrightLift Eng Mgr), Diego Ruiz (BrightLift MLOps)

Summary: Quick live demo of the Redwood Hosted Gen API and Console Optimize. Showed streaming behavior, how to tune params for retail chat, retries, and a short tour of the Console Optimize suggestions (batching, caching, quantization recommendations).

[00:00] Alex: All right everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex Morgan from Redwood, AE on the account, joining with Priya our SE. How are you all?
[00:08] Marcus: Good, thanks. Excited to see the demo, we've been looking at options for chat responses in our support flows.
[00:12] Sara: Yep, trying to keep latency under 200ms for first token ideally, but we'll compromise.
[00:18] Priya: Great, I'll kick off with a quick overview of streaming behavior then we'll jump into console and some Optimize tips. Quick note — if anything sounds off in the transcript I typed fast, so apologies for typos.
[00:30] Priya: So Redwood's Hosted Gen API supports streaming responses - you get tokens as they're generated. That helps perceived latency. We can tune initial inject size, token chunking, and set stop sequences. For retail chat you'd usually set a shorter max_tokens and lower temperature to keep answers concise.
[00:48] Marcus: When you say "token chunking" do you mean batching on the server side, like continuous batching?
[00:52] Priya: Exactly — continuous batching. The runtime groups requests for similar seq lengths to improve throughput. Console Optimize will suggest a batching window based on your 95th percentile latency.
[01:10] Sara: Any gotchas with history? We keep a 6-message context, sometimes longer. Will that blow up latency?
[01:16] Priya: It depends. Long contexts increase KV cache sizes and memory. We recommend prefix caching for static system prompts and only append recent user turns. Also, you can pin a shorter conversation length in the call to reduce token count.
[01:30] Diego: Is prefix caching automatic? I saw something about K-V cache in docs but wanted clarity.
[01:34] Priya: Yes, there's automatic KV cache reuse across streaming calls in a session — the runtime reuses cached key values when you pass the conversation id. In the console it's surfaced under Optimize -> Cache suggestions (sometimes mislabeled in older docs as K-V "cash" so ignore that typo).
[01:50] Marcus: Ha good to know. On retries — what's your recommended backoff pattern? We're worried about duplicate outputs if we retry too aggressively.
[01:57] Alex: Good question. We recommend idempotency tokens on request creation. For transient network errors, exponential backoff with jitter. For partial streams (e.g., connection drop after 60% tokens) the client should detect partial completion and either resume using the same idempotency key or re-request with a prompt that includes the last confirmed token. Priya, do you want to show the example?
[02:18] Priya: Sure, I have a quick snippet in the sandbox. (screen share) Here we set idempotency_key on create and include resume_token for long streams. If you can't resume, fallback to a shorter re-gen with a summary of the partial output to avoid repetition.
[02:40] Marcus: Resume sounds tricky for our frontend. If resume isn't feasible, would you recommend falling back to a smaller model or different param set?
[02:48] Priya: Yep, that's the graceful degradation pattern — fallback to a lower-cost compat model or reduce max_tokens and temperature to keep latency down. Console Optimize can auto-suggest model variants per route based on cost/latency SLOs.
[03:05] Sara: What's the default retry TTL? Like how long will the runtime keep the session info for resumes?
[03:10] Priya: Hosted keeps short lived session state — typically 10 minutes for KV cache by default, configurable per tenant for Dedicated. We can extend for Private setups but it affects memory.
[03:22] Diego: On the console tour, can you show where batching and cache tuning appear?
[03:26] Priya: Sure — switching to the Console. (brief pause) Dashboard -> Optimize -> Live Recommendations. Here you'll see suggested batch size, target latency, and predicted cost delta. For your workload the console is suggesting a 32ms batching window and to enable prefix cache for the support system prompt.
[03:50] Marcus: The 32ms window — won't that add latency? We're worried about adding too much headroom for the first token.
[03:55] Priya: It's a balance. The window waits up to the configured ms to collect requests; if you have steady traffic that increases throughput, it reduces cost. For low traffic routes you can set dynamic policies: immediate dispatch for new users, batching for background tasks.
[04:10] Sara: Any immediate safety defaults? Like content filtering or guard rails?
[04:14] Alex: We include model safety tools and response filters; you can also add post-generation checks in the pipeline. We'll share our safety deck. Note some of the labelling in the console references Redwood "SafetyNet" in older screenshots which is a stale name — docs will be updated.
[04:35] Marcus: On security, our security team needs SOC 2 and SSO compatibility. Do you support SAML SSO and audit logs?
[04:41] Alex: Yes, Hosted supports SSO integrations (SAML/SCIM) at the account level and we provide audit logs. For Dedicated/Private you get more control and integration options. We'll send the SOC2 summary and network diagram after the call.
[04:58] Diego: Does Hosted encrypt at rest with customer KMS?
[05:02] Priya: Hosted uses provider-managed keys by default but we support customer-managed keys (KMS) on Dedicated and Private. There's a roadmap item to offer Bring-Your-Own-Key for Hosted for some enterprise tiers.
[05:16] Marcus: Great. Can you show a quick live gen example with streaming so we can see token cadence?
[05:22] Priya: Yep — switching to the sandbox code. (runs a prompt) You'll see tokens stream in; note the initial latency is dominated by model warmup if this route is cold. For warm routes the first token comes faster.
[05:40] (tokens appear)
[05:45] Sara: The cadence looks smooth. How do we measure and alert on partial streams?
[05:50] Priya: In Console -> Observability you can set alerts on incomplete streams and token mismatch rates. We also provide per-route token histograms.
[06:02] Marcus: If we set conservative params, will we degrade quality? For scripted answers we can be deterministic but for help desk we want some variation.
[06:10] Priya: For deterministic outputs set lower temp and top_p, and you can use sampling with a fixed seed in some models. For support, maybe temp 0.2-0.4, top_p 0.8. Keep max_tokens short and prefer system prompt templates to reduce hallucination.
[06:30] Diego: Any advice on token counting and cost? We saw a spike in tokens in our initial tests.
[06:35] Alex: Two common causes: verbose system prompts and verbose customer history. Use templated system prompts and compress history with summaries. Console Optimize has a token-usage tab that highlights high-cost prompts.
[06:50] Marcus: I heard about quantization — does Redwood do that automatically?
[06:54] Priya: We support quantized model variants for Dedicated and some Hosted variants; Console Optimize can recommend switching to an int8 variant when quality delta is acceptable. Quantization reduces cost but can increase latency a bit depending on hardware.
[07:10] Sara: Let's talk about endpoints — do we route by region? We need EU data residency for some flows.
[07:15] Alex: Yes, routing by region is supported. For EU residency you can use a region-restricted Hosted tenant or Dedicated in EU. Private on-prem is available for strict residency. We'll note your regulatory needs in the deal.
[07:30] Marcus: For the sandbox test, can we run a short benchmark comparing two param sets?
[07:34] Priya: Absolutely. I'll attach a perf script that runs 500 warm + 500 cold requests and captures P50/P95 for first token and full response, plus token counts.
[07:46] Diego: Perfect. On retries one more question: if client auto-retries without idempotency key, do you dedupe?
[07:54] Priya: If there's no idempotency key, retry can create duplicate generations. We strongly recommend idempotency_key for create calls and to check response status codes. We also provide idempotency helpers in our SDK.
[08:10] Marcus: Any limits on streaming length? We sometimes have long transcripts for returns.
[08:15] Priya: There's a per-request max token cap; for very long content we recommend chunking and summarization every N turns. Also consider embeddings for retrieval augmented flows to avoid re-sending full history.
[08:32] Sara: Can the Console show route-level costs so our finance team can map to product features?
[08:36] Alex: Yes, per-route cost breakdowns and token-level cost are available. You can export CSVs for finance.
[08:45] (brief pause - screenshare moves)
[09:02] Priya: Quick note — the sandbox includes a preconfigured route that demonstrates graceful degradation: it falls back to a compat model when latency > threshold. I'll point you to the config.
[09:18] Marcus: Nice. What's typical warmup time for a model? We've seen wide variance.
[09:22] Priya: For modern LLMs warmup to first token varies from ~80ms to 300ms depending on model size and whether it's been recently invoked on that host. Autoscaling and warm pools help for Dedicated.
[09:40] Diego: For our expected 200 reqs/min peak, does Hosted handle that scale or do we need Dedicated?
[09:47] Alex: Hosted can handle bursts and scale, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower P95 for consistent high-volume workloads. Based on your numbers we can model cost both ways — I'll include a comparison.
[10:05] Marcus: Can you explain how the console recommends quantization? Is it purely cost-based?
[10:10] Priya: It's multi-metric — cost, measured quality delta on evals, and latency. The console shows predicted delta if you switch to a quantized variant and points to failing eval prompts.
[10:28] Sara: We're also concerned about compliance logging — how detailed are audit logs?
[10:32] Alex: Audit logs include API calls, user actions in the console, and model versions served. We can turn on extended logging for Dedicated/Private with longer retention.
[10:44] Marcus: Any mention of limit throttles? We have a brittle front-end that can't handle sudden 429 spikes.
[10:49] Priya: We provide rate limiting and recommended client-side backoff. Also we provide a per-route token budget to prevent runaway costs and 429s.
[11:02] Diego: Great. Let's cover the concrete next steps so we have owners.
[11:06] Alex: Action items — I will send hosted vs dedicated pricing and the SOC2 summary. Priya will send sandbox setup and the perf script. Diego will confirm access list. Marcus/Sara will review and confirm timeline.
[11:22] Marcus: Sounds good; target to start sandbox Monday 6/29 if we get the access.
[11:27] Alex: Perfect. Anything else?
[11:30] Sara: One small thing — can the console flag when a model variant was updated? We need that for reproducibility.
[11:35] Priya: Yes, model versioning is tracked in the console and we can export the rollout history. There's a small UI bug that shows it at the bottom of the timeline, but functionally it's available.
[11:48] Marcus: Thanks everyone.
[11:50] Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the benchmark.
[11:55] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription had a few mis-heard terms (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of "KV cache"), minor speaker attribution inconsistencies.
